```shiploop-state
{
  "evidence_refs": [
    "request S1 (tool and its three figures)",
    "request S2 (tests)",
    "exercise statement: repository empty, no tools, no files, unattended run",
    "stage guidance items 1-8 and the Done-when list"
  ],
  "headline": "Intake maps both request sentences to one greenfield stdlib Python CLI plus tests, records 7 defaulted open questions (CSV schema first), and states that the outcome is visible in the repo only after final return.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "summary": "Legend: [F]=fact from the request or exercise; [A]=assumption, recorded as a default.

OUTCOMES
S1 outcome: a Python command-line tool that reads one or more CSV files of sales records and prints one summary with total revenue, revenue per region and units per product [F]. Reading: total revenue = grand sum; revenue per region = revenue summed by region; units per product = units summed by product [A].
S2 outcome: an automated test suite delivered with the tool, covering the three figures and the input-error paths [F that tests are wanted; the coverage list is A, see Q7].

BOUNDARIES
S1 boundary, repository and run scope: the repository is empty, so this is greenfield with no existing code, conventions, CI or data to preserve [F]. The run is unattended [F]. Scope is the tool plus its tests and nothing else [F]. Not included: packaging or publishing, CI config, README beyond --help, per-file or time-series reports, top-N, JSON/CSV/HTML output, GUI or web [A].
S1 boundary, user constraints: Python is required [F]. Standard library only (argparse, csv, decimal), so the run needs no network or installs [A].
S1 boundary, authority: the request names the thing to write (a tool, in this repository), and that is the grant. It covers creating the tool and tests as files in the run's isolated checkout, returned to the source repository at final return [A]. It does not cover installing packages, network use, push, release, publishing, or modifying or copying any real sales data. Input CSVs are read-only [A].
S1 boundary, consumers and entry points: a person or shell script runs `python -m salessummary FILE [FILE...]` and reads stdout, stderr and the exit status [A]. The module name is a default. Tests are run from the repo root with `python -m unittest` [A].
S2 boundary: tests use only small synthetic fixture CSVs created in temp dirs, never real sales data [A].
Prior run: the request does not continue an earlier run and the repository is empty, so no prior-run or recovery guidance applies [F].
Risks: (1) the CSV schema is unknown, and a wrong guess means the tool fails on the requester's real files, which is the main risk; (2) float arithmetic on money; (3) silently skipping bad rows would produce wrong totals; (4) tests that only mirror the implementation; (5) currency and locale unknown, so no currency symbol is printed.

INTERACTION AND STATE (CLI, one-shot)
Actors: whoever runs the process, identified only by the OS user, with no auth [A]. Shared state across people, devices or sessions: none [A]. Lifetime: a single process run, which ends at exit; nothing persists [A]. Hidden from whom: nothing is hidden. The tool prints aggregates only and never writes files [A]. Runtime already provides: argv, stdin/stdout/stderr, exit codes, the filesystem, and the Python stdlib csv/decimal/argparse [F]. This rules out a database, cache, config file, server, prompts, credentials and multi-user concerns.

OPEN QUESTIONS (owner -> what it blocks)
Q1, from S1 'sales records' (schema undefined). Owner: discovery first, then a recorded default. Discovery must establish whether any sample CSV, schema doc or export description exists (likely none in an empty repo) and whether revenue is a column or is units x unit price. Default: UTF-8 (BOM tolerated), comma-delimited, header row required; columns region, product, units, plus either revenue or unit_price (revenue = units x unit_price when there is no revenue column); header match case-insensitive and trimmed; extra columns ignored. Rules out headerless files, other delimiters or encodings, and column-mapping flags. Blocks: parser, revenue computation, every test fixture.
Q2, from S1 'files' plural vs 'a summary' singular. Owner: recorded default. Default: all files given as arguments are merged into one combined summary; at least one file is required; no stdin and no directory handling beyond what the shell expands. Rules out per-file breakdowns. Blocks: CLI argument shape, multi-file tests.
Q3, from S1 'prints'. Owner: recorded default. Default: plain text on stdout in three labelled sections, money with 2 decimals and no currency symbol, rows sorted by descending value then name so output is deterministic. Rules out structured or formatted-table output. Blocks: output assertions in tests.
Q4, from S1 (numeric handling and bad input). Owner: recorded default. Default: Decimal for money and integers for units; negative values (returns) summed as-is; header-only file gives zero totals and exit 0; a malformed row (missing or non-numeric field), a missing or unreadable file, or a missing required column prints file:line context to stderr, prints no summary, and exits nonzero. Rules out a lenient skip-with-warning mode. Blocks: error-path tests and exit codes.
Q5, from S1 (grouping keys). Owner: recorded default. Default: region and product values are whitespace-trimmed and otherwise matched exactly (case-sensitive); an empty region or product counts as malformed (Q4). Blocks: grouping tests.
Q6, from S1 (environment and layout). Owner: discovery of the run environment (python3 version, whether pytest exists), else a recorded default. Default: python3 stdlib only, package `salessummary/` with `__main__.py`, and `tests/` at the repo root; tests written with unittest, pytest-compatible. Blocks: the plan stage's file layout and the verify stage's test command.
Q7, from S2 'Add tests'. Owner: recorded default. Default: unit tests for aggregation plus end-to-end CLI runs on synthetic fixtures, covering happy path, multi-file, header-only, malformed row, missing file and decimal rounding; no coverage threshold. Blocks: the verify stage's pass criterion.

DISCOVERY SOURCE HINTS (leads, not verified facts)
No team, workspace, channel, site, private repository or owner is named in the request, and the repository is empty, so none are invented. Leads: the requester's sales or finance export (sample CSVs or schema docs) that produces the 'sales records'; the run environment's python3 and test runner. Ambiguous terms to resolve: 'sales records' (columns, header, encoding), 'revenue' (column vs units x price, gross vs net, currency), 'region' (own column vs derived from country or state), 'product' (name vs SKU), 'units' (integer vs fractional). No sensitive locator exists. If real sales data turns up, keep its locator in an authorized private store, never in KNOWLEDGE/, which is committed.

WHERE AND WHEN VISIBLE
Where it must become usable: this repository, as a tool runnable from a checkout via the command line, plus its tests [A]. The request names no deployment target, package index or release, so nothing awaits a release [F]. When: the files first exist in the run's isolated checkout once the implementation stage writes them, and the test results are visible in the verify stage's evidence and report. The source checkout (the empty repository) stays at its snapshot until the run's final return. Only after that return are the tool and tests visible and usable in the repository itself.

COVERAGE CHECK: S1 -> outcome, boundaries, Q1-Q6; S2 -> outcome, Q7, risks. Every open question names its owner and what it blocks, and visibility is stated."
}
```
